question: What is the atomic number of Bohrium which is named after physicist Niels Bohr, one of the founders of quantum theory?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 107.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bohrium (Bh) is a synthetic chemical element with atomic number 107, placed in Group 7 of the periodic table as a transition metal. (बोहरियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 107)

 

• It was first synthesised in 1981 by a German research team at the GSI Helmholtz Centre in Darmstadt, led by Peter Armbruster and Gottfried Münzenberg.

 

• The element is named in honour of the Danish physicist Niels Bohr, one of the principal architects of quantum theory and the Bohr model of the atom.

 

• Bohrium is highly radioactive with no stable or naturally occurring isotopes; it exists only in laboratory-produced, extremely short-lived forms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Elements named after physicists in the same region of the periodic table include Rutherfordium (104), Seaborgium (106), Meitnerium (109) and Copernicium (112).

 

• Bohrium belongs to the group of superheavy transactinide elements, all of which are synthetic.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (117): Atomic number 117 belongs to Tennessine (Ts), not Bohrium.

 

• Option 3 (113): Atomic number 113 belongs to Nihonium (Nh).

 

• Option 4 (101): Atomic number 101 belongs to Mendelevium (Md), named after Dmitri Mendeleev.

question: Under the Koppen climate classification system, which climate zone is generally located on the western coasts of continents, receiving rainfall between 35 - 90 cm?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mediterranean Climate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mediterranean climate (Koppen type Cs) occurs on the western margins of continents, roughly between 30° and 45° latitude in both hemispheres, and receives annual rainfall of about 35 - 90 cm. (भूमध्यसागरीय जलवायु — पश्चिमी तटीय क्षेत्र)

 

• It is characterised by hot, dry summers and mild, wet winters, with rainfall concentrated in the winter months due to the shifting of westerlies and subtropical high-pressure belts.

 

• Classic examples include the Mediterranean Sea region, central Chile, the Cape Town region of South Africa, south-western Australia, and California.

 

• The natural vegetation associated with this climate is sclerophyllous (hard-leaved) evergreen scrub, known locally as maquis, chaparral, or fynbos.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mediterranean lands are often called the "world's orchard" because of their suitability for citrus fruits, olives, grapes and figs.

 

• The corresponding climate on the eastern margins of continents at similar latitudes is the Humid Subtropical (Cwa/Cfa) climate.

 

NOTE

 

• Humid Subtropical Climate (Option 2): Found on the eastern coasts of continents, with rainfall throughout the year (often summer-dominant), e.g. south-eastern USA, southern China.

 

• Subtropical Steppe Climate (Option 3): A semi-arid climate found in continental interiors adjoining hot deserts, with much lower and more erratic rainfall.

 

• Highland Climate (Option 4): Determined by altitude rather than coastal position, showing rapid vertical changes in temperature and rainfall.

question: The following represent the opportunity cost of holding money, EXCEPT:
option_1: loss of utility from goods that could have been purchased from the same amount of money
option_2: loss of interest earning on cash holdings
option_3: loss of purchasing power of money due to inflation
solution_text:
The correct answer is transaction cost in withdrawing money.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The opportunity cost of holding money refers to what a person gives up by keeping wealth as idle cash instead of investing it or spending it. (धन धारण की अवसर लागत — नकद रखने की लागत)

 

• Holding cash means foregoing interest that could have been earned by depositing or investing that money, which is a direct opportunity cost.

 

• Holding cash also means the purchasing power of that money erodes due to inflation, and it means giving up the utility/satisfaction of goods that could otherwise have been bought with it right away.

 

• Transaction costs in withdrawing money, however, are costs of converting other (less liquid) assets into cash — i.e., a cost of NOT holding money in liquid form. Holding money actually avoids this cost rather than being a cost of holding it, so it is the exception.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This concept underlies Keynes' liquidity preference theory, where people hold money for transaction, precautionary and speculative motives, each carrying its own opportunity cost.

 

• The desire to avoid transaction costs (of converting bonds/assets to cash) is itself one of the motives for holding money, reinforcing that it is not a cost of holding money.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1: Correct example of an opportunity cost — money not spent means foregone utility from goods.

 

• Option 2: Correct example of an opportunity cost — cash held earns no interest.

 

• Option 3: Correct example of an opportunity cost — inflation erodes the real value of cash held.

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason for excessive cold in north India?
option_2: Cold winds from the Caspian Sea
solution_text:
The correct answer is Equatorial current.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• North India experiences severe cold in winter mainly because of its continental location (large distance from the moderating influence of the sea) and the arrival of cold winds from Central Asia, including the region of the Caspian Sea. (उत्तर भारत — शीत ऋतु के कारण)

 

• The snow-covered Himalayas further intensify winter cold in the adjoining plains by radiating cold air (katabatic winds) into North India, while also blocking cold Siberian winds from Central Asia to a large extent.

 

• An "equatorial current" is an oceanic current concept, found in the world's oceans near the equator, and has no bearing on North India's continental winter climate.

 

• Because North India is far from any moderating equatorial ocean current, this option does not explain the region's cold winters at all — making it the correct "NOT a reason" choice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The western disturbances originating over the Mediterranean Sea also bring winter rainfall and cold waves to North-West India.

 

• Coastal areas of India, being closer to the sea, experience a more moderate winter compared to the continental interior and north.

 

NOTE

 

• Distance from sea (Option 1): A genuine reason — continental locations have larger temperature extremes.

 

• Cold winds from the Caspian Sea (Option 2): A genuine reason — cold continental winds from Central Asia lower temperatures in North India.

 

• Snowfall in the Himalayas (Option 3): A genuine reason — snow-covered mountains intensify the cold of adjoining plains.

question: When camphor is heated, which of the following changes will take place?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Solid to gas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Camphor is a substance that undergoes sublimation — it changes directly from the solid state to the gaseous (vapour) state on heating, without passing through the liquid state. (कपूर — ऊर्ध्वपातन)

 

• This is why solid camphor placed in the open gradually disappears/shrinks over time, releasing its characteristic aromatic vapour directly into the air.

 

• Sublimation occurs because the intermolecular forces in camphor are weak, allowing molecules to escape directly from the solid surface into vapour at ordinary atmospheric pressure upon heating.

 

• Other common substances that sublime include naphthalene (mothballs), iodine, ammonium chloride and dry ice (solid CO2).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The reverse process — gas directly changing to solid — is called deposition.

 

• Sublimation is used industrially and in laboratories as a purification technique to separate sublimable substances from non-sublimable impurities.

 

NOTE

 

• Solid to liquid to gas (Option 2): This describes ordinary melting followed by boiling/evaporation, not sublimation — not applicable to camphor.

 

• Liquid to gas (Option 3): This is simple vaporisation/boiling, which requires the substance to already be a liquid; camphor starts as a solid.

 

• Solid to liquid (Option 4): This describes melting alone, which is not what happens to camphor on heating.

question: Who among the following personalities is associated with synthesising classical and modern Indian dance through a theatre group called Ranga Sri Little Ballet Troupe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shanti Bardhan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Shanti Bardhan was a pioneering Indian choreographer and dancer who founded the Little Ballet Troupe (Ranga Sri) in Bombay in 1952, blending classical Indian dance forms with modern theatrical and folk elements. (शांति बर्धन — लिटिल बैले ट्रूप)

 

• He had earlier trained under Uday Shankar at the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre, Almora, which shaped his vision of a modern, syncretic Indian dance-theatre.

 

• His most celebrated work with the Little Ballet Troupe was "Ramayana", a dance-drama that used masks, puppetry-inspired movement and group choreography to reinterpret classical themes for a modern stage.

 

• The Little Ballet Troupe became one of independent India's most influential dance-theatre companies, nurturing many later choreographers and dancers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Uday Shankar, Shanti Bardhan's mentor, is regarded as the father of modern Indian dance and founded his own India Culture Centre at Almora.

 

• The Little Ballet Troupe's productions combined music, mime, mask work and classical technique, a hallmark of Bardhan's innovative style.

 

NOTE

 

• Guru Bipin Singh (Option 1): A renowned exponent and reviver of Manipuri dance, not associated with the Little Ballet Troupe.

 

• Pandit Birju Maharaj (Option 2): A legendary Kathak maestro of the Lucknow Kalka-Bindadin gharana.

 

• Remo Fernandes (Option 4): A well-known Indian pop/rock musician and singer, unrelated to classical/modern dance synthesis.

question: What is the distance between the hurdles in 100 m women's hurdles in metres?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.50.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the women's 100 m hurdles, athletes clear 10 hurdles, each 84 cm (0.84 m) high, spaced 8.50 metres apart. (100 मीटर बाधा दौड़ — बाधाओं के बीच 8.50 मीटर)

 

• The distance from the start line to the first hurdle is 13.00 m, and the distance from the last hurdle to the finish line is 10.50 m.

 

• The event tests a sprinter's speed combined with technical hurdling rhythm, typically requiring 3 strides between hurdles.

 

• These specifications are laid down by World Athletics for standard outdoor track and field competitions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• In the men's 110 m hurdles, the hurdle height is 1.067 m, with hurdle spacing of 9.14 m.

 

• In the 400 m hurdles (both men and women), there are 10 hurdles spaced 35 m apart, with hurdle heights of 91.4 cm (men) and 76.2 cm (women).

 

NOTE

 

• 7.50 (Option 1), 9.00 (Option 2) and 8.00 (Option 3) do not correspond to the official inter-hurdle spacing of 8.50 m prescribed for the women's 100 m hurdles.

question: Which of the following Indian Para Canoeists won the bronze medal in the 2022 International Canoe Federation's Paracanoe World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prachi Yadav.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Prachi Yadav, an Indian para-canoeist from Madhya Pradesh, won the bronze medal in the VL2 200m category at the 2022 International Canoe Federation (ICF) Paracanoe World Cup. (प्राची यादव — पैराकैनो विश्व कप कांस्य पदक)

 

• With this achievement, she became the first Indian para-canoeist to win an international medal in the sport of paracanoeing.

 

• She took up para-canoeing after suffering a spinal injury and has since represented India at multiple international paracanoe events.

 

• Her achievement helped bring visibility to paracanoeing, a relatively new competitive sport for India at the international level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Paracanoeing is a Paralympic sport, contested in kayak (KL) and va'a (VL) boat classes for athletes with different disability classifications.

 

• Prachi Yadav has also received honours, including being felicitated by the state government, for her pioneering achievement in the sport.

 

NOTE

 

• Ramya Smruti (Option 1), Sarita Rao (Option 2) and Pranshi Rawal (Option 4) are not associated with the bronze medal win at the 2022 ICF Paracanoe World Cup; the medal was won by Prachi Yadav.

question: The threshold limit for total income eligible for rebate under Section 87A has been increased from ₹5,00,000 to ₹________ for assesses opting for the new tax regime as per the Finance Bill 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 7,00,000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the Finance Bill 2023 (Union Budget 2023-24), the rebate under Section 87A of the Income Tax Act, for individuals opting for the new tax regime, was raised so that taxpayers with total income up to ₹7,00,000 pay no income tax. (धारा 87A छूट — नई कर व्यवस्था में सीमा ₹7,00,000)

 

• Earlier, under the previous provisions, this rebate limit stood at ₹5,00,000 (applicable mainly under the old tax regime).

 

• This change was announced by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman while presenting the Union Budget 2023-24 on 1 February 2023, and it made the new tax regime the default regime from FY 2023-24 onward.

 

• The move was aimed at making the new, simplified tax regime (with fewer exemptions/deductions but lower slab rates) more attractive to individual taxpayers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Budget 2023 also revised the tax slabs under the new regime to six slabs and raised the basic exemption limit to ₹3,00,000.

 

• The standard deduction of ₹50,000 was also extended to salaried taxpayers and pensioners under the new tax regime for the first time in Budget 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• 11,00,000 (Option 2), 8,00,000 (Option 3) and 10,00,000 (Option 4) do not match the revised Section 87A rebate threshold of ₹7,00,000 announced in the Finance Bill 2023.

question: Which of the following Commissions was appointed by Lord Curzon to enquire into the working of the police administration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Frazer Commission.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lord Curzon, Viceroy of India, appointed the Indian Police Commission of 1902, chaired by Sir Andrew Fraser, to enquire into the working of the police administration across British India. (फ्रेज़र आयोग — पुलिस प्रशासन जांच)

 

• The Commission's recommendations led to important reforms, including the establishment of the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) in each province and of the Central Intelligence Bureau at the national level.

 

• It also recommended raising police pay and improving training, though many of its recommendations were only partially implemented.

 

• Curzon's tenure (1899-1905) was marked by several such administrative and educational commissions aimed at reorganising British Indian institutions.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lord Curzon is also known for the Partition of Bengal (1905) and for setting up the Indian Universities Commission (1902), chaired by Thomas Raleigh.

 

• The Police Act of 1861, enacted after the 1857 revolt, had earlier laid the basic framework of police administration that the 1902 Commission sought to review.

 

NOTE

 

• Kitchener Commission (Option 1): Lord Kitchener, as Commander-in-Chief, was involved in army reorganisation, not police reform.

 

• Hunter Commission (Option 2): The Hunter Commission is best known for inquiring into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre (1919), and an earlier Hunter Commission (1882) dealt with education.

 

• MacDonnell Commission (Option 4): Not associated with police administration reform under Curzon.

question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of fundamental duties mentioned in the Indian Constitution?
option_1: There is a legal sanction against their violation.
option_3: They are part of the Indian tradition.
option_4: They are not sacrosanct or permanent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is There is a legal sanction against their violation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Duties, listed under Article 51A in Part IV-A of the Constitution, are non-justiciable — there is no direct legal/constitutional sanction (penalty) for their violation, unlike Fundamental Rights. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — विधिक रूप से प्रवर्तनीय नहीं)

 

• They were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, inspired partly by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR.

 

• Fundamental Duties are essentially moral and civic obligations of citizens (e.g., to respect the Constitution, protect the environment, promote harmony), making them civic duties in nature.

 

• They also draw upon values already embedded in Indian tradition, mythology and philosophy (e.g., respect for nature, communal harmony), and, being subject to amendment by Parliament, they are not sacrosanct or permanent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• There were originally 10 Fundamental Duties; the 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added an 11th duty — for parents/guardians to provide educational opportunities to children aged 6-14 years.

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights (Part III), which are enforceable through Article 32/226, Fundamental Duties have no corresponding enforcement mechanism in the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• They are civic duties (Option 2): This IS a genuine feature of fundamental duties, so it is not the answer.

 

• They are part of the Indian tradition (Option 3): This IS a genuine, correct feature, so it is not the answer.

 

• They are not sacrosanct or permanent (Option 4): This IS a genuine, correct feature (they can be amended), so it is not the answer.

question: Name the Indian who won the title at the World Chess Armageddon Asia & Oceania event in Berlin, Germany in April 2023.
solution_text:
The correct answer is D Gukesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian Grandmaster D Gukesh won the title at the World Chess Armageddon Asia & Oceania event, held in Berlin, Germany in April 2023. (डी गुकेश — शतरंज आर्मागेडन एशिया व ओशिनिया चैंपियन)

 

• The Armageddon Championship Series is a rapid/blitz-format chess event organised as part of the global qualification pathway leading to the Chess.com/Champions Chess Tour ecosystem, with regional legs held across continents.

 

• Gukesh's win in the Asia & Oceania leg qualified him for the corresponding global Armageddon finals.

 

• At the time, Gukesh (born 2006) was rapidly rising through world chess rankings and went on to become World Chess Champion in 2024, defeating Ding Liren.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gukesh became the youngest player to cross a FIDE rating of 2750 and later the youngest ever undisputed World Chess Champion in December 2024.

 

• India has produced several young chess prodigies in this era, including R Praggnanandhaa, Nihal Sarin, Arjun Erigaisi, alongside Gukesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Abhimanyu Mishra (Option 1): An American Grandmaster (of Indian origin) known as the youngest GM in history; he did not win this event.

 

• R Praggnanandhaa (Option 2): A leading Indian GM, notable for reaching the 2023 FIDE World Cup final, but he was not the winner of this particular Armageddon Asia & Oceania title.

 

• Nihal Sarin (Option 3): A strong Indian GM known for rapid/blitz chess, but not the winner of this event.

question: Under the current regulatory framework, what is the maximum tenure of a microfinance loan in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 36 months.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the RBI's Regulatory Framework for Microfinance Loans (2022), a microfinance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household with annual income up to ₹3,00,000. (सूक्ष्म वित्त ऋण — अधिकतम अवधि 36 माह)

 

• As per this framework, such loans are generally structured with a maximum tenure of 36 months, keeping in view the repayment capacity of low-income borrowers.

 

• The 2022 framework replaced the earlier NBFC-MFI-specific rules with a harmonised, activity-based regulation applicable across all regulated entities lending microfinance loans (banks, NBFCs, NBFC-MFIs, etc.).

 

• It also removed the earlier interest rate caps/margin caps, replacing them with a board-approved policy for pricing, while continuing to emphasise borrower protection through disclosure and over-indebtedness safeguards.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The RBI's earlier 2011 NBFC-MFI norms had specified a minimum tenure of 24 months for loans above ₹15,000, along with caps on the number of MFIs lending to a single borrower.

 

• The 2022 harmonised framework also introduced a household income-based repayment cap, limiting total monthly loan repayment obligations to 50% of household monthly income.

 

NOTE

 

• 24 months (Option 1): This was the minimum, not maximum, tenure specified under the earlier (2011) NBFC-MFI regulations.

 

• 12 months (Option 2) and 18 months (Option 3): Neither matches the maximum tenure figure prescribed under the current framework.

question: Which of the following states has the highest poverty rate in India, according to the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• According to NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, Bihar recorded the highest proportion of multidimensionally poor population among Indian states, at roughly 51.9%. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक — बिहार सर्वाधिक गरीब राज्य)

 

• The MPI is based on the globally-recognised Alkire-Foster methodology, measuring poverty across three dimensions — health, education and standard of living — using 12 indicators.

 

• Jharkhand ranked second-highest in poverty rate, followed by Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh, all featuring among the states with the largest poor populations.

 

• The MPI report is jointly prepared by NITI Aayog, in technical partnership with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and UNDP, using data mainly from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• States/UTs with the lowest MPI poverty rates include Kerala, Goa and Puducherry.

 

• A follow-up NITI Aayog discussion paper noted that roughly 13.5 crore Indians moved out of multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Had a high poverty rate but ranked below Bihar and Jharkhand.

 

• Jharkhand (Option 2): Recorded the second-highest MPI poverty rate, after Bihar.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Had a large absolute number of poor people (given its large population) but a lower poverty rate (percentage) than Bihar.

question: Who among the following singers became the first Indian folk artist to attend the Cannes Film Festival 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mame Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mame Khan, the celebrated Rajasthani folk singer, became the first Indian folk artist to open/represent India on the red carpet at the Cannes Film Festival, in May 2022. (ममे खान — कान फिल्म समारोह में प्रथम भारतीय लोक कलाकार)

 

• He is renowned for popularising Manganiyar folk music of Rajasthan on national and international platforms, including Bollywood songs like "Kesariya Balam" and "Chaudhary".

 

• His appearance at Cannes 2022 was seen as a landmark moment for Indian folk music and traditional artists gaining recognition on a global cinematic stage.

 

• Mame Khan has also received a National Film Award nomination/recognition for playback singing and continues to perform Rajasthani folk music worldwide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Cannes Film Festival is one of the world's most prestigious annual film festivals, held in Cannes, France.

 

• India has had growing representation at Cannes in recent years, including designer/actor appearances and Indian films in official selections.

 

NOTE

 

• Gurudas Man (Option 1): A well-known Punjabi folk singer, not associated with this Cannes 2022 first.

 

• Daler Mehendi (Option 2): A popular Indian pop singer, not a folk artist associated with this Cannes achievement.

 

• Teejan Bai (Option 3): A celebrated Pandavani folk singer from Chhattisgarh and Padma Vibhushan awardee, but not the artist who attended Cannes 2022 in this context.

question: Which of the following is India's first all-women-managed railway station?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gandhinagar Railway Station, Jaipur.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gandhinagar Railway Station in Jaipur, Rajasthan, was declared India's first all-women-managed railway station, with all operational roles — station master, ticket booking, RPF staff — handled by women. (गांधीनगर रेलवे स्टेशन, जयपुर — प्रथम महिला-प्रबंधित रेलवे स्टेशन)

 

• The initiative was launched by the North Western Railway (NWR) zone, aimed at promoting women's empowerment within Indian Railways.

 

• The station became operational under all-women management around 2018, and has since served as a model replicated to some extent at other stations.

 

• This step was part of a broader Indian Railways push to increase representation of women in operational and safety-related roles.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has since seen other women-centric railway initiatives, including all-women train crews on select routes.

 

• Matunga Railway Station, Mumbai, is separately notable as India's first station with an all-women staff on the Central Railway suburban network in a different, earlier initiative — but Gandhinagar (Jaipur) holds the broader distinction as the country's first fully all-women-managed station.

 

NOTE

 

• Chennai Egmore Railway Station (Option 1): A major historic terminus in Chennai, not known as an all-women-managed station.

 

• Trivandrum Central Railway Station (Option 3): A major station in Kerala, not associated with this distinction.

 

• Matunga Railway Station, Mumbai (Option 4): Notable for an all-women staff initiative on Mumbai's suburban network, but Gandhinagar, Jaipur, is credited as India's first all-women-managed station overall.

question: Which of the following personalities is a well-known Indian plant physiologist and physicist?
solution_text:
The correct answer is JC Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose (JC Bose) was a pioneering Indian physicist, biologist/plant physiologist and biophysicist, celebrated for his work on radio waves and plant physiology. (जगदीश चंद्र बोस — पादप शरीर विज्ञानी एवं भौतिकशास्त्री)

 

• He invented the crescograph, an instrument to measure the growth response of plants to stimuli, providing experimental evidence that plants have sensitivity/feelings and respond to external stimuli like animals.

 

• Bose is also credited as a pioneer of wireless/radio communication research, having demonstrated microwave transmission before Marconi's famous experiments, though he did not patent his inventions.

 

• He founded the Bose Institute in Kolkata (1917), one of India's oldest research institutes, dedicated to interdisciplinary scientific research.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• JC Bose was one of the first Indian scientists to receive international scientific recognition and a Fellow of the Royal Society.

 

• A crater on the Moon is named after him, honouring his contributions to science.

 

NOTE

 

• CV Raman (Option 2): Nobel laureate physicist known for the Raman Effect in light scattering, not primarily a plant physiologist.

 

• CNR Rao (Option 3): Renowned Indian chemist, known for solid-state and materials chemistry, and a Bharat Ratna awardee.

 

• JRD Tata (Option 4): Legendary Indian industrialist and aviation pioneer, founder of Tata Airlines (later Air India), not a scientist in this field.

question: In the Indian Constitution, which of the following Articles deals with the right to move to the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental rights?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 32.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 32 of the Indian Constitution guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, empowering citizens to move directly to the Supreme Court for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. (अनुच्छेद 32 — संवैधानिक उपचारों का अधिकार)

 

• Dr. B.R. Ambedkar famously called Article 32 the "heart and soul" of the Constitution, as it makes Fundamental Rights meaningful and enforceable.

 

• Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue writs — habeas corpus, mandamus, prohibition, certiorari and quo warranto — for enforcing Fundamental Rights.

 

• A parallel provision, Article 226, empowers High Courts to issue similar writs, but their jurisdiction is wider (covering both Fundamental Rights and other legal rights) while Article 32's Supreme Court jurisdiction is specifically tied to Fundamental Rights.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The right under Article 32 itself is a Fundamental Right, included in Part III of the Constitution, and cannot ordinarily be suspended except during a National Emergency under Article 359.

 

• Article 32 falls within the broader group of Articles 12-35 that together constitute the Fundamental Rights chapter of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 30 (Option 1): Deals with the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions.

 

• Article 33 (Option 3): Empowers Parliament to modify Fundamental Rights in their application to armed forces and police personnel.

 

• Article 31 (Option 4): Originally dealt with the right to property; it was repealed by the 44th Amendment (1978) and property is now only a legal right under Article 300A.

question: Kamsale is the folk dance of which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kamsale is a traditional folk dance-and-music form from Karnataka, particularly associated with the Mysore region and devotees of the deity Male Mahadeshwara. (कमसाले नृत्य — कर्नाटक)

 

• The dance derives its name from the "kamsale", a pair of metallic cymbal-like percussion instruments that performers clash together rhythmically while dancing and singing devotional songs.

 

• It is traditionally performed by groups of male dancers who move in synchronised, energetic formations, often as part of religious processions and temple festivals dedicated to Mahadeshwara.

 

• Kamsale is recognised as an important element of Karnataka's folk performing arts heritage, showcasing a blend of devotion, music and acrobatic movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable folk dances of Karnataka include Dollu Kunitha (drum dance) and Veeragase.

 

• The Male Mahadeshwara Hills (MM Hills) in Karnataka is an important pilgrimage centre linked to the folklore and devotional tradition behind Kamsale.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Known for folk dances like Chhau and Jhumair, not Kamsale.

 

• Kerala (Option 3): Known for classical/folk forms like Kathakali, Theyyam and Mohiniyattam, not Kamsale.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Known for folk dances like Jat-Jatin and Domkach, not Kamsale.

question: Which of the following was NOT a goal of the Five-Year Plans?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Security.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Five-Year Plans of India, formulated by the Planning Commission, traditionally pursued four principal, widely-cited goals: Growth, Modernisation, Self-reliance and Equity. (पंचवर्षीय योजनाएं — प्रमुख लक्ष्य)

 

• Growth referred to increasing the country's capacity to produce goods and services (raising GDP/national income).

 

• Self-reliance meant reducing dependence on imports, particularly for food grains and capital goods, especially emphasised from the Third and Fourth Plans onward.

 

• Equity meant ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reached all sections of society, reducing inequality and poverty; "Security" was not one of the standard four goals of India's Five-Year Plans as formally articulated in NCERT/economic planning literature.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Modernisation, the fourth commonly cited goal (alongside growth, self-reliance and equity), referred to adopting new technology and changing the structural/institutional set-up of the economy.

 

• India's Five-Year Plans ran from 1951 (First Plan) until the 12th Plan (2012-2017), after which the Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog.

 

NOTE

 

• Self-reliance (Option 1), Equity (Option 2) and Growth (Option 3) are all genuine, well-established goals of India's Five-Year Plans, so none of these is the correct "NOT a goal" answer.

question: Ambubachi fair is held every year in which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ambubachi Mela is an annual Hindu festival held at the Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, Assam, celebrating the annual menstruation cycle of the goddess Kamakhya. (अंबुबाची मेला — कामाख्या मंदिर, असम)

 

• The fair is typically observed in the monsoon month of Ashadha (mid-June), when the temple remains closed for three days, believed to represent the goddess's menstrual period, and reopens with grand celebrations on the fourth day.

 

• The Kamakhya Temple is one of the most important Shakti Peethas in India, revered by Tantric practitioners and devotees of the goddess.

 

• Thousands of pilgrims, sadhus and tantrics from across India gather at Kamakhya for this unique fertility-related festival.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ambubachi Mela is sometimes referred to as the "Mahakumbh of the East" due to the scale of pilgrim gathering.

 

• Assam is home to several other important religious and cultural festivals, including Bihu, the state's principal harvest festival.

 

NOTE

 

• Manipur (Option 1): Known for festivals like Lai Haraoba and Sangai Festival, not Ambubachi.

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 2): Known for festivals like Ziro Festival of Music and tribal harvest festivals, not Ambubachi.

 

• Nagaland (Option 3): Known for the Hornbill Festival, not Ambubachi.

question: Which of the following is NOT a primary function of commercial banks?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Transfer of funds.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The primary functions of commercial banks are traditionally classified as (a) accepting deposits from the public and (b) lending loans/advances (which results in credit creation). (वाणिज्यिक बैंकों के प्राथमिक कार्य — जमा स्वीकार करना व ऋण देना)

 

• "Transfer of funds" — such as remitting money between accounts or locations via cheques, drafts, NEFT/RTGS, etc. — is classified as a secondary (agency) function of banks, not a primary one.

 

• Secondary functions are further divided into agency functions (e.g., fund transfer, collecting cheques/bills, acting as trustee) and general utility functions (e.g., issuing letters of credit, safe deposit lockers, underwriting).

 

• Since primary functions strictly refer to the core deposit-taking and credit-creating role of banks, transferring funds falls outside this core definition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Credit creation by commercial banks, based on the fractional reserve system, is a distinctive primary function that allows the banking system to expand the overall money supply.

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), as the central bank, regulates commercial banks' credit creation through tools like the CRR, SLR and repo rate.

 

NOTE

 

• Creation of credit (Option 2): A genuine primary function, arising from the deposit-lending cycle of banks.

 

• Lending loans to the public (Option 3): A genuine, core primary function of commercial banks.

 

• Receiving deposits from the public (Option 4): A genuine, core primary function of commercial banks.

question: Which biosphere was declared as India's 16th Biosphere Reserve in 2009, noted for the conservation of Red Fox, Blue Rock Pigeon and Lammergeier?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cold Desert.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve, located in Himachal Pradesh, was notified as India's 16th Biosphere Reserve in 2009. (कोल्ड डेजर्ट बायोस्फीयर रिजर्व — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• It encompasses the Pin Valley National Park, Chandratal and Sarchu wildlife areas, and the Kibber Wildlife Sanctuary, representing the unique trans-Himalayan cold desert ecosystem.

 

• The reserve is noted for its distinctive high-altitude fauna, including the Red Fox, Blue Rock Pigeon, Lammergeier (bearded vulture), along with species like the Snow Leopard, Ibex and Tibetan Wolf.

 

• Its landscape features sparse vegetation, extreme cold and high-altitude cold-arid terrain typical of the trans-Himalayan biogeographic zone.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• India currently has a network of Biosphere Reserves under UNESCO's Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme, several of which (like Nilgiri, Sundarbans, Nanda Devi) are internationally recognised.

 

• The Cold Desert region is also important for its unique high-altitude cultural landscape, including Spiti Valley's Buddhist monasteries.

 

NOTE

 

• Seshachalam (Option 2): A biosphere reserve in Andhra Pradesh, known for red sanders forests, not the answer here.

 

• Agasthyamalai (Option 3): A biosphere reserve spanning Kerala and Tamil Nadu, in the Western Ghats, unrelated to this cold-desert ecosystem.

 

• Dehang Debang (Option 4): A biosphere reserve in Arunachal Pradesh, in the eastern Himalayas, not associated with these species/this declaration.

question: What is the basic difference in the aggregates at market price and factor cost?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Net indirect taxes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Market Price (MP) and Factor Cost (FC) are two ways of valuing national income aggregates, and they differ by the amount of Net Indirect Taxes (NIT), where NIT = Indirect Taxes − Subsidies. (बाजार मूल्य व साधन लागत — शुद्ध अप्रत्यक्ष कर का अंतर)

 

• The relationship is expressed as: Market Price = Factor Cost + Net Indirect Taxes, or equivalently, Factor Cost = Market Price − Net Indirect Taxes.

 

• Indirect taxes (like GST, excise duty) raise the market price above the factor cost, while subsidies lower the market price below what producers actually receive, so the net adjustment factor is Net Indirect Taxes, not gross indirect taxes alone.

 

• This distinction is fundamental in national income accounting, ensuring that measures like GDP at market price and GDP at factor cost are properly reconciled.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Depreciation is instead the factor that distinguishes Gross aggregates from Net aggregates (e.g., GDP vs NDP), not market price from factor cost.

 

• Since the 2015 revision of India's national accounts by the CSO/MoSPI, GDP is officially estimated at market prices, replacing the earlier factor-cost-based headline measure.

 

NOTE

 

• Depreciation (Option 1): Relevant to Gross vs Net distinction, not Market Price vs Factor Cost.

 

• Indirect taxes (Option 2): Only part of the adjustment; subsidies must also be netted out, making "Net Indirect Taxes" the precise, complete answer.

 

• Direct taxes (Option 4): Direct taxes (like income tax) do not enter into the market price vs factor cost distinction at all.

question: Who was the first to mention the incident of Jauhar in Persian?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Amir Khusrau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Amir Khusrau, the celebrated Indo-Persian poet and chronicler at the court of Alauddin Khilji, is credited as the first writer to mention the incident of Jauhar in Persian literature, in his work "Khazain-ul-Futuh". (अमीर खुसरो — जौहर का प्रथम फारसी उल्लेख)

 

• He describes the Jauhar committed by the women of Chittor during Alauddin Khilji's siege and conquest of the Mewar fort in 1303 CE.

 

• Jauhar refers to the act of mass self-immolation by women (along with, at times, children) to avoid capture, dishonour or enslavement following the defeat of their menfolk in battle, a practice recorded at several Rajput forts.

 

• Amir Khusrau's works are prized as near-contemporary historical sources for the Khilji period, blending poetic style with chronicling of political and military events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Amir Khusrau is also renowned as the "father of Qawwali" and is credited with introducing several Persian and Turkish poetic forms into Indian literary tradition.

 

• Later, more elaborate Rajput/bardic accounts of the Chittor Jauhar (linked to Rani Padmini) emerged much later in works like Malik Muhammad Jayasi's "Padmavat" (16th century), a work of legend rather than a contemporary Persian chronicle.

 

NOTE

 

• Ibn Batutah (Option 1): A Moroccan traveller who visited India later (14th century) and wrote travel accounts (Rihla), not the first to record Jauhar in Persian.

 

• Ziauddin Barani (Option 3): A noted historian of the Delhi Sultanate (author of "Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi"), writing somewhat later than Khusrau's account of this event.

 

• Hasan Nizami (Option 4): Author of "Taj-ul-Ma'asir", chronicling the early Delhi Sultanate (Qutb-ud-din Aibak's era), predating the Chittor Jauhar of 1303 and unrelated to its first mention.
